findings.title: importCustomer callers without a tenant map now silently drop all tenantExternalIds memberships
findings.failure: importCustomer is exported and called with only { record } by importThreads.ts:140, importThreadMessage.ts:150 and importAllCustomersAndUsersInRecords.ts:59. The old code did the tenants lookup inline for every customer with tenantExternalIds. The new code does `args.tenantsByExternalId ?? new Map()`, so for those callers the map is empty, tenantsToLink is [] and importCustomerTenantMemberships is never called. Thread, message and bulk record imports of CRM customers that carry tenantExternalIds create or update the customer but never link them to tenants, with no error and no log. The PR description claims 'Single-customer callers keep the per-customer lookup', which the code does not do.
findings.fix: Keep the per-customer getTenantsFromIdentifiers fallback in importCustomer when args.tenantsByExternalId is undefined (build the map from that lookup and keep the old scope.fail on error), and only use the map when supplied. Add a litest that calls importCustomer without a map and asserts the memberships.
findings.evidence: git grep importCustomer: importThreads.ts:140 `importCustomer(ctx, { record: recordCustomer })`, importThreadMessage.ts:150, importAllCustomersAndUsersInRecords.ts:59. importCustomers.ts:327 `const tenantsByExternalId = args.tenantsByExternalId ?? new Map<string, Tenant>();` replaced the deleted lookup block (base lines ~301-307 with `if (lookupResult.isErr) return scope.fail(...)`). The new test only exercises importCustomers (batch).

findings.title: NOOP fast path ignores importedByJobDefinitionId, so re-imports by a new job definition never claim the customer
findings.failure: shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate takes a third argument importedByJobDefinitionId and returns true when it differs from customer.importedByJobDefinitionId (shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.ts:17-22, covered by its unit tests lines 105-111). The old path called it through updateCustomerUnsafe with the argument (customerAggregate.ts:1026-1033). The new fast path calls it with two arguments, and importCustomers passes importedByJobDefinitionId through upsertCustomer args. For the common import case (onUpdate has no email or company, existing customer unchanged) the fast path now returns NOOP and customerDb.updateCustomer never writes imported_by_job_definition_id (customerDb.ts:951). Customers that already exist (created manually, by another job definition or before this column was set) are no longer attributed to the current job definition on re-sync, where before they were.
findings.fix: Pass importedByJobDefinitionId as the third argument in the fast path: shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate(existing, onUpdate, importedByJobDefinitionId). Add a litest where an existing customer is upserted with a different importedByJobDefinitionId and assert it is updated.
findings.evidence: customerAggregate.ts:659-660 calls with two args; destructured importedByJobDefinitionId is in scope at :635; helper lines 11-22 of shouldPerformCustomerUpsertUpdate.ts. The new litests in customerAggregate.litest.ts do not cover a differing job definition id.

findings.title: Failed tenant lookup chunk is swallowed and turns real tenants into 'absent'
findings.failure: getTenantsByExternalId logs a warn and `continue`s when getTenantsFromIdentifiers errors (DB timeout, pool exhaustion, permission error), then returns Result.ok with a partial map. Previously a lookup error did scope.fail for that record. Now every customer whose tenants were in the failed chunk is treated as having no matching tenant: with shouldSkipTenantlessCustomers it is recorded as skipped 'None of the tenantExternalIds exist in our database' (a misleading permanent looking skip), otherwise the customer is saved with no tenant memberships. The sync reports success and the next sync is not necessarily re-run for unchanged customers. Under write load (the stated motivation) transient failures are the likely case.
findings.fix: Return Result.err on the first chunk failure (and let importCustomers return Result.err, which the caller at :513-515 already handles), so the batch fails and retries instead of silently skipping/unlinking.
findings.evidence: importCustomers.ts:280-283 `ctx.log.warn(...); continue;`, function always returns Result.ok at :288; the caller's isErr branch at :513 is therefore unreachable. The type comment at :297 'a missing key means no such tenant exists' makes the partial map indistinguishable from true absence.

findings.title: Fast path adds an extra SELECT to every create and real update, and removes the read from the transaction
findings.failure: When the customer is missing or actually changed, the fast path reads the customer outside a transaction and then the transaction reads it again at :668. For first time syncs and changed customers this is one extra query per record on the same writer, and the NOOP decision is made on a pre transaction snapshot so a concurrent update between read and return yields a stale 'NOOP' customer. The in tx path had the same unlocked read, so correctness risk is equal, but the cost is not offset when the hit rate on unchanged customers is low (first sync, backfills).
findings.fix: Verify the NOOP ratio on production before merge (the PR cites no number), and consider reusing the first read to skip the second SELECT inside the transaction.
findings.evidence: customerAggregate.ts:645-649 vs :668-674 both call customerDb.getCustomerByIdentifier with selectForUpdate false.

findings.title: Fast path gating is wider than the stated rationale and unavailable for email or company updates
findings.failure: Only upserts where onUpdate.email and onUpdate.companyId are both undefined take the fast path. The import path builds onUpdate via parseImportCustomer; if it sets email on update (customers synced with an email) the optimization never applies and the transaction count does not drop. The PR does not show that the import path leaves email undefined.
findings.fix: Confirm in parseImportCustomer that onUpdate omits email for CRM imports, or measure transactions per second after deploy; otherwise the headline write load reduction does not materialise.
findings.evidence: customerAggregate.ts:645 `if (onUpdate.email === undefined && onUpdate.companyId === undefined)`; email update path still opens withTransaction at :666.

findings.title: getTenantsByExternalId returns a Result that can never be an error
findings.failure: The function only ever returns Result.ok, so the isErr branch in importCustomers (:513-515) is dead code and the Result wrapper misleads readers into assuming errors propagate (see swallowed chunk finding).
findings.fix: Either propagate the error (preferred) or return the Map directly and drop the dead branch.
findings.evidence: importCustomers.ts:271-289 single return Result.ok(tenantsByExternalId); no Result.err in the body.

checked_fine: getTenantsFromIdentifiers dedupes and does a single ANY query per chunk (tenantAggregate.ts:511-520, tenantDb.ts:259); chunk size 500 is safe.
Batch tenant lookup in importCustomers covers only records with tenantExternalIds, matching the per record branch condition in importCustomer.
uniq on tenantExternalIds preserves the old result set; old lookup also deduped via uniq in getTenantsFromIdentifiers.
Fast path permission check happens before the new read; customerId identifier not found falls through to the existing transaction path and keeps the entityNotFound error.
NOOP path emits no domain event, same as the previous NOOP result in updateCustomerUnsafe.
